name: Name
title: Waking the Dead: Part 1
body: By Aeryn Rudel

name: Name
body:
Colonel Jeremiah Kraye sat behind his desk in the CRS headquarters in Highgate. The papers and documents piled up in front of him were as numerous as the aches and pains that infested his fifty-seven-year-old body. He was only a few years past the saddle, a few years beyond firing his Radcliffe carbine and swinging his mechanikal saber Bitter End from the back of a charging horse. Now, both rifle and sword collected dust on the wall above him. No less relics than their owner.
A knock sounded at the door to Kraye’s needlessly voluminous office. "Come," he said, eager for any distraction at all from the field reports burying his desk.
The door opened, and Kraye’s aide-de-camp, Swift Sergeant Gerrold Haines, entered. Haines looked uncomfortable in his spotless uniform, but the empty right sleeve would keep him out of a ranger’s field kit until he was approved for a mechanikal prosthesis. He’d lost the arm fighting the Orgoth at Orven, and by all accounts he had acquitted himself bravely both before and after the gruesome injury.

name: Name
body: "Sorry to bother, sir," Haines began, "but I have an odd report I think you should see." He stepped forward and placed a single sheet of paper atop the pile on Kraye’s desk. Kraye fished out his reading glasses, put them on, and picked up the report. He scanned it, frowned, then looked up at Haines. "Has Lord General Turpin returned from Caspia?" *** Lord General Evelyn Turpin was ten years younger than Kraye, but her mastery of Caspian politics had accelerated her ascent into the highest echelons of military command. Kraye stood in her office at the Third Army garrison, the room a massive space festooned with shining honors, polished awards, and spotless weapons. "You think the intelligence from this"—she glanced down at the report—"Captain Shadowtongue is credible? He’s a notorious pirate." "He is that, ma’am," Kraye said, "but a pirate who risked his ship and his life to bring us this information. Not much in it for him—unless he’s telling the truth." Turpin shrugged. "Perhaps this Shadowtongue encountered what he thought was a Cryxian blackship carrying what he thought was a Cryxian warcaster—one who matches no description of known Cryxian leaders— who he thought was being delivered in secret to our shores, for what he says is an unknown but dire purpose. To be blunt, that's a hell of a lot of guesswork, wouldn't you say?"

name: Name
body: Kraye took a deep breath. "Ma’am, in the field, I learned to trust my gut. If something felt off, that’s because it was off. Call it intuition, a hunch, whatever you want, but it kept me alive and our enemies on their heels for some thirty years." "And I suppose your intuition is telling you this pirate’s story is accurate?" Turpin said. "Just let me send a reconnaissance unit to investigate," Kraye said. "We’ll learn the truth in days." Turpin said nothing for a moment, and then, "We have increased patrols by over three hundred percent along the western coast." "I’m aware, ma’am, but—" Turpin held up a hand. "In the estimation of the CRS, Colonel, what is the chance a lone blackship could land undetected anywhere in Cygnar at the moment?" "Slimmer than usual," Kraye conceded through clenched teeth. "Then it is my estimation that the CRS should be chasing facts, not figments." Turpin pushed the report back at Kraye. "Dismissed." *** "I’m sorry, sir," Sergeant Haines said as he and Kraye left Lord General Turpin’s office. "It’s not my place to say so, but Lord General Turpin is wrong to ignore this."

name: Name
body:
"You’re right—it’s not your place." Kraye flashed the young swift sergeant a smile. "Your penance will be to draft a letter for me to an old friend, Colonel Jarvinson."
"The commander of Westwatch, sir?"
"The very one."
A knowing smile crept over Haines’ face. "At once, sir."

name: Name
body: Wraithbinder Nekane stood on the deck of the blackship The Ripping Fang, staring into the fog-wreathed night. The necrotite glow from her warcaster armor splashed the silver mist with lurid green, giving the impression that she was standing in the midst of a putrescent snowstorm. . A wrenching cough pulled Nekane’s attention to a towering figure striding up from the hold. Captain Aiakos was a hulking, battle-scarred human in equally battle-scarred warcaster armor. He crossed the deck and stood beside Nekane, stinking of sweat, spilled blood, and burning necrotite. Life and death intertwined. Aiakos coughed again, turned, and spat a glob of glistening black phlegm onto the deck. The putrid mass writhed with pale green maggots. Necrotite poisoning was inevitable for the living servants of the Nightmare Empire, and Aiakos had been breathing the scorched fumes from his armor and helljacks for decades. Just as Nekane had. Aiakos wiped his mouth with the back of a gauntleted hand. "Head north from our landing site. The Orgoth are waiting at the mouth of the Banwick River."

name: Name
body: "Land ho!" one of The Ripping Fang’s sailors called out, and a sliver of shadow appeared in the fog. It gained substance and form as the shoreline loomed. *** The fog had begun to lift by the time The Ripping Fang made landfall. The ship was amphibious, a vessel designed for both naval combat and quick, bloody shore raids. The landing ramp descended, and Nekane watched her small task force move from the darkness of the Ripping Fang’s hold and into mist-filtered moonlight. The bulk of her troops were comprised of mechanithralls, animated corpses fitted with a variety of blades, saws, and axes. Among the mechanithralls were several sludge thralls armed with bile cannons that spewed a caustic effluvium strong enough to melt steel and the flesh beneath it. The thralls were led by a skarlock lieutenant, Chemosh, an autonomous undead creature possessing higher-than-normal levels of intelligence and will. The final members of Nekane’s task force were no simple thralls. She felt the pull of her warjack Hades’ crude, rage-filled consciousness press against her own. The helljack stalked from the blackship’s hold, a looming monstrosity of spiked iron and gangrenous Cryxlight.

name: Name
body: To me, she urged, and Hades’ massive, tusked head turned in her direction. It pounded across the sand to her side, pulsing hatred and hunger into her brain. Next came the three ancient wraiths known as the Furies. Anathan, Dogreth, and Valak floated upon baleful green eddies of deathly power, the empty armor that made up their corporeal forms ensorcelled to bind their souls to Caen. The dread spirits were loyal to Nekane, and she had a keen understanding of such creatures gained from her tutelage under the eldritch Goreshade. The binding and controlling of wraiths, shades, and other incorporeal horrors was a skill few in the Nightmare Empire possessed, and it had been key to Nekane’s rise. Finally, Chatterbane, Nekane’s necrotech, scuttled out of the hold, his augmented necromechanikal form clattering noisily. He made a beeline to Hades and immediately began fussing over the helljack. "Hades is operating within acceptable parameters," Chatterbane said, his high, plaintive voice causing Nekane to clench her teeth. "But the third phalangeal digit requires sharpening, and due to the cramped confines I have been unable to properly maintain the soul cannon since we left Blackwater. I will see to them as soon as possible."

name: Name
body:
"That can wait," Nekane said. "Recalibrate Hades’ furnace for silent running. See to the thralls as well as my armor and your own furnace."
"Such a recalibration will make Hades sluggish and your armor much heavier." Chatterbane sighed. Then the necrotech looked her up and down. "Can you bear it? The living tire easily."
Nekane rolled her eyes. Though a gifted necrotech, Chatterbane possessed a number of irritating peculiarities. Paramount among them was a bigoted view of the living, whom he considered both inferior and disgustingly inefficient. "What I can bear is none of your concern. Do as I say. Now."
"As you wish." Chatterbane began making the adjustments to Hades’ furnace.
With the task force on the shore, Captain Aiakos approached Nekane. Beneath the glow of his armor’s furnace, his skin had a sickly, jaundiced hue, though it was not just the Cryxlight that gave him his corpse-like pallor. "There are Cygnaran patrols all over the coast. Keep your smoke low and move only at night, and you shouldn’t gather unwanted attention."

name: Name
body:
"And if I do?" Nekane said.
"Don’t leave any evidence," Aiakos said.
"Captain, what do you know of Nine Stone?" Nekane asked. The ancient ruin was one of the sites she’d been tasked to scout. She was to ascertain if it contained fell energies sufficient to build the Well of Annihilation, an ancient Cryxian design believed to be powerful enough to pull even a god from Urcaen, all to satisfy the terms of Dominarch Deneghra’s alliance with the Orgoth.
"A dangerous place," Aiakos answered. "If the blackclads find you there, you’ll wish a battalion of Cygnaran soldiers had found you instead. The Devourer cultists are not kind to intruders."
Nekane smiled. "That sounds . . . promising."

name: Name
body:
To Nekane, Nine Stone looked like the hand of a vengeful god rising from the earth, maybe to pull the world down into some endless darkness. She could feel the power, rich and terrible, thrumming through the place as they approached it.
The fog had lifted completely by the time they reached the ruins, and the night was clear and vast. Caen’s three moons watched from above, and the nearby ocean crashed and roared in the distance.
Nine Stone was more than just the dagger-like pillars that gave it its name. It was a sprawling ruin of crumbling walls, ancient earthworks, and, reputedly, a collapsed system of tunnels beneath the ruins, tunnels built for unguessable purposes. Its origin was unknown, but the Orgoth avoided it during their initial occupation, and only the Devourer cults and their druids invoked its power any longer.
"Much death and suffering here," Chatterbane said excitedly. "If one were so inclined, one could sink a necrotite mine."
Nekane nodded. It was a credible notion. Though her primary task was to find a location to build the Well of Annihilation, she was also on the lookout for sites suitable for other Cryxian endeavors.  "Take samples. If there is necrotite in the area, it may make a good spot for extraction."

name: Name
body: Chatterbane held up a drill-shaped apparatus, which he proceeded to affix to the end of one of his mechanikal appendages. "I have just the thing." He trundled off into the dark, muttering happily to himself. Nekane summoned the Furies to her side and pointed at the ruin. "Search for anything living." "We obey," Anathan hissed. "Your will," Dogreth whispered. "And none other," Valek finished. The three wraiths drifted toward the ruins. To Chemosh, her Skarlock lieutenant, Nekane said, "Take the thralls and create a perimeter. If you see any signs of the enemy, report to me at once. Do not engage." Chemosh bowed and left to do her bidding. At length, Nekane stood alone with only Hades beside her for a moment, luxuriating in the roiling maelstrom of aggression that filled the helljack’s cortex. After a time, the Furies reappeared out of the darkness. "Only the dead remain," the wraiths said in unison. "Much power there," Dogreth said. "Perhaps too much," Anathan said. Valek was silent, the empty void beneath his helmet somehow accusatory, as if he wished to finish her sister’s thought with for one such as you.

name: Name
body: The wraiths were given to dire pronouncements. Not exaggeration per se, more a strange theatrical bent. Still, their warnings could not be completely ignored. She gestured at them. "Follow me. Stay close." *** The moment Nekane set foot in Nine Stone, she was nearly overcome by the raw power of it. The crumbling walls and ramparts were suffused with dire, chaotic strength, but the nine monoliths radiated a magical potency as strong as dragon fire. Her attunement to incorporeal undead was an element of her Iosan heritage and one reason Deneghra had chosen her for this mission. Not only could she sense and direct the necrotic energies of incorporeal spirits, but she could also detect magic associated with death to a degree few others in the Nightmare Empire could. Deneghra had recognized Nekane’s unique power and how it might help them both achieve their goals. Nekane approached the towering stones. She removed the gauntlet from her left hand and reached out, placing her living flesh against one of the great black pillars.

name: Name
body:
It was like stepping into the heart of a volcano. Power surged through her, and a flood of distorted images assaulted her mind. Stone knives flashed beneath a blood red moon, screams of pain and exultation howled on the wind, and writhing entities of pure darkness rose up from hellish depths. The power was incredible, ancient, and absolutely untamable.
With a strangled cry, Nekane wrenched herself away from the pillar and fell back onto the ground. Her breath came in quick, ragged gasps; her head throbbed. Surely  there was more than sufficient energy here to power to extract the god Morrow  from Urcaen, but who could control it? There was a pall of metaphysical chaos that hung over the place, a legacy of countless years of ineffable magic. It was not the kind of sorcery that could be bent and shaped to her will. It simply would not serve.
She felt another presence enter the ruins. As she lurched to her feet, she saw Chemosh hurrying in her direction.
"Report," she said.
"A Cygnaran patrol, ten strong, Storm Knights," Chemosh said. "They are headed here."

name: Name
body: "Can we outrun them?" Chemosh shook his head. "They are mounted." "Pull the thralls into the ruins. We will fight here." Nekane raced to the edge of the ruins where Hades waited, a trickle of necrotite smoke issuing from his stacks. She was no necrotech, but she understood the basics of necro-mechanika. With a few adjustments, she turned Hades’ furnace up to full stoke, and the helljack came alive in a burst of green Cryxlight, his presence blooming in her mind like an exploding star. Let them come. *** The tell-tale blue glow of storm chambers lit the nighttime horizon like an azure sunrise. Nekane had positioned herself, Hades, Chatterbane, Chemosh, and the Furies within the center of the nine monoliths. They were the bait that would draw the Cygnarans in. Then the thralls, hidden throughout the ruins, would surround them and strike. The thunder of steel-shod hooves arose from the north end of Nine Stone. The storm lance legionnaires appeared, heavily armored warriors astride destriers in plate barding. Storm capacitors shed a fierce blue light from the units attached to each Cygnaran’s back and from the fearsome mechanika lances they carried.

name: Name
body:
The Cygnaran soldiers saw Nekane, lowered their lances, and charged. The legionnaires covered roughly half the distance between themselves and the nine monoliths before the hidden thralls burst from cover and attacked from all directions, miring the Cygnaran advance in an avalanche of undead flesh and scything steel.
Pulses of galvanic energy discharged in all directions, some finding their marks, blasting apart mechanithralls in showers of sparks and decayed flesh. Nekane winced. She had precious few military resources to squander . She had to end the battle quickly.
She ordered Hades into a loping run and followed in the helljack’s wake, urging it forward and directly into the first legionnaire. Hades tore the man’s horse out from beneath him with a swipe of a death claw and the legionnaire crashed to the ground. The man tried to rise and bring his lance to bear, but Hades impaled him with its tusks and pitched his limp corpse over its shoulder.
There were still five legionnaires left, and they’d formed a tight circle, lances pointed outward in a hedge of voltaic death. They focused their first volley on Hades, hitting the helljack with a concentrated burst of galvanic pulses. The volley sent it staggering back, exposing Nekane for a brief moment.

name: Name
body: One of the storm lances, seeing an opportunity for valor and victory, broke formation and charged Nekane. The Furies circled around Nekane in a protective ring, but she waved them away. "No, he’s mine." Nekane aimed the rune thrower attached to her left vambrace and fired. A rune-scribed spike struck the legionnaire high in the shoulder, and his outline shuddered as fell magic surged through him. He became insubstantial, ghost-like, and Nekane pulled the phantom Cygnaran forward off his mount. He became corporeal again seconds later, dropping to the ground in a heap. His mount, spooked, reared and bolted. Grinning, Nekane fired her rune caster again as the storm lance struggled to his feet. The bolt struck, and again, his form shimmered, and again she pulled him closer. She could now see his face beneath his helmet, pale, horror stricken. When he regained corporeality, she fired again, and ripped his screaming shade toward her, phantom blood cascading down his armor, his lance dragging behind him useless and forgotten. He fell before her, became solid flesh, and she plunged the hellspike on her gauntlet into his throat.

name: Name
body:
The legionnaire gurgled and died at her feet. Nekane looked up to see that the mechanithralls and Chemosh had made short bloody work of the remaining legionnaires and their mounts. A pile of slashed bodies and torn armor was all that remained, but so many dead was damning evidence of their presence.
Nekane’s mind worked feverishly at the problem of hiding the battle. There was no perfect solution, so she would make do.
"Pile the bodies and horses and use the bile cannons on them," she said to Chemosh. The caustic eluvium fired by the sludge thralls’ weapons would reduce the armor and flesh to unrecognizable slag. "Then bury what remains. Do it quickly. We must leave this place at once."
Chemosh left to carry out her orders. The acid stench of bile cannons filled Nekane’s nose moments later, and soon there was nothing left of their enemies but a gray slurry. With the tireless and single-minded devotion of the undead, the mechanithralls began to dig into the hard earth with their weapons, and within a short while had buried the mass of dissolved armor and flesh.

name: Name
body: "Do you think this was one of the patrols Captain Aiakos spoke of?" Chatterbane said as he bolted on a blue-armored plate to Hades’ hull to repair a bit of damage. Nekane didn’t. "No. This felt more deliberate. Directed." With all that Aiakos had said about Nine Stone, it seemed the Cygnarans would avoid the place. A blessing maybe that it was not suitable for her purposes. Minutes later, her forces diminished, Nekane left the ruins of Nine Stone and headed east along the Banwick River. Beyond, the Wyrmwall Mountains loomed. There was another site there she would examine, but first, she had a more diplomatic function to attend to. The Orgoth warlord Sabbreth was waiting for an update regarding the bargain she had made with Deneghra, and Nekane was to deliver it. From all accounts, this Sabbreth was violent, reckless, and unpredictable. The perfect ally, Nekane thought acidly as she moved northeast toward the Wyrmwalls through the predawn gloom.

name: Name
body: From Nine Stone, Nekane traveled north toward the site where she was to meet Sabbreth at the mouth of the Banwick River. A fiery red glow on the horizon marked the location of the Orgoth encampment. There were eight of the Orgoth warships dragged up onto the broad bank, and both troops and strange, feral warjacks moved among them. Nekane estimated this raiding party was made up of roughly three hundred soldiers and a half a dozen warjacks. As Nekane’s retinue approached the Orgoth encampment, a trio of towering Orgoth warriors barred their path. Each sentry was clad in archaic plate armor with fur or leather at joints and gorget, and they were armed with shields and curved blades. They looked primitive and brutal. "Who goes?" one of the Orgoth warriors said in heavily accented Cygnaran. "I am Wraithbinder Nekane, vassal of Dominarch Deneghra. I have come to confer with Sabbreth, the Eternal Annihilation." Chatterbane chuckled beside her. "Eternal Annihilation. Such ridiculous titles. What does that even mean?"

name: Name
body:
The Orgoth warrior sized Nekane up—she had apparently not heard Chatterbane’s comment—and snorted. "You are small for one who leads."
Nekane surged forward, her hellspike springing from its wrist mount. She shoved the blade up under the Orgoth warrior’s chin, where there was flesh between gorget and helm. "And you speak much for one who follows."
The Orgoth warrior chuckled and held up her hands, waving off her compatriots who had drawn their weapons. "My apologies, Wraithbinder. I spoke in haste. I will take you to Mistress Sabbreth at once."
Nekane sheathed her hellspike and stepped back.
"This way," the Orgoth warrior said and motioned for Nekane to follow.
Though she had a rudimentary understanding of Orgoth technology gleaned from Cryxian spies, Nekane had never encountered the invaders’ blaze core technology in person. The fiery red glow from weapons and the infernal engines driving the Orgoth warjacks was like a strange reflection of Cryxian necromechanika. She couldn’t help but wonder why they’d gone down this path—it seemed so much cruder than the helljack and bonejack designs they had so obviously copied.

name: Name
body:
"Ugh, look at the brutish things," Chatterbane said, scuttling alongside Nekane. The necrotech waved an appendage at a towering Orgoth warjack with a horned head and a hull bristling with spikes and blades. "There are rumors they bind the spirits of beasts into these abominations. Nonsense, of course, but if such a thing were possible, the results could be . . . fascinating."
Nekane said nothing. In truth, she saw more than a few similarities between her helljack and the Orgoth machines.
With stares and muttered words, the warriors in the Orgoth encampment made note of Nekane’s procession of undead. That was the key difference between them: the Orgoth sought salvation and continued life through servitude to their infernal masters. The Nightmare Empire offered undeath as the path to preserve one’s power and control for eternity. It could be said they were two sides of the same coin, though Nekane knew which side she preferred.
As they neared the greatest of the Orgoth warships, its landing ramp descended and from out of the hold came their host. Sabbreth, who was called the Eternal Annihilation, was tall and robust, and the incandescent light of blaze energy shone from various points on her armor and burned brightest from an apparatus on her back—the Orgoth equivalent of a necrotite furnace.

name: Name
body: A pair of warjacks—feral things shaped like great beasts of metal and blood—flanked the Orgoth warlord, snarling and clawing at the ground as if barely under their mistress’ control. Nekane urged Hades to stand beside her. She’d turned the helljack’s furnace up to full stoke, and green Cryxlight and crimson blaze fire met and clashed as Sabbreth drew near. The Orgoth warlord removed her crested helmet, revealing a narrow face with large expressive eyes, a wide clear brow, and short-cropped black hair. Her lips were turned down in a frown, and she drew in a deep breath through her nose before she spoke. "You are Deneghra’s servant?" Sabbreth said in a low, commanding tone. Then, oddly, the Orgoth warlord repeated the question. "Deneghra’s servant?" This time, her voice was higher, rougher, as if someone else entirely had spoken. Nekane wasn’t sure what to make of the strange display. "I am Wraithbinder Nekane, and I was sent on the order of Dominarch Deneghra." She didn’t like the term servant, but the Orgoth likely viewed everyone in terms of servants and masters. "I am to find a suitable location that serves our mutual purposes."

name: Name
body: "And this meager force is all you brought with you?" Sabbreth said, waving a dismissive hand at Nekane’s assembled thralls. The warlord’s face twitched, and she said something else under her breath, but Nekane could not hear it. "I lead a scouting party," Nekane said. "My mission, as I said, is to scout out a site with enough power to serve both our needs. I cannot pass through enemy territory with an army at my back." "I will bolster your numbers with soldiers and warjacks." Sabbreth’s lips curled up in a patronizing smile. "So that you might better succeed at your mission." The smile faded, and the warlord’s voice changed again, this time lilting, almost flowery. "Take it as a sign of our commitment to the others’ cause." "She’s bloody mad," Chatterbane said, once again living up to the first part of his name. He’d at least had the sense to say it in Iosan, so Sabbreth was unlikely to understand. Nekane couldn’t help but agree with the necrotech, and Deneghra had warned her as much. Sabbreth had possession of an artifact known as the Lash of Horva, and by all accounts, the device was slowly destroying her mind. "I need nothing more than to update you on my progress, assure you that the Dominarch and I are committed to our arrangement, then carry on."

name: Name
body: "Progress?" Sabbreth said. "What progress?" "I surveyed the ruins known as Nine Stone shortly after I landed on these shores. There is much power there, but it is unsuitable for our needs." "Our needs, or yours?" Sabbreth said. Her mien had changed, and she seemed more in control. "Nine Stone is known to us. There is enough strength in that place to challenge a god." "Strength, yes, but not strength you or I can control," Nekane said. "I bade a dragon rip its own heart from its body, and it laid its athanc at my feet before it died," Sabbreth said. "What do you know of my strength?" The threat in the warlord’s words stained the air between them, and Nekane knew she was at a pivotal point. She could not show weakness. She took a step toward Sabbreth. "If you can use the power at Nine Stone to accomplish your goal"—She stepped even closer, until she could feel the warlord’s breath on her face—"then do it." Nekane stared into Sabbreth’s eyes and felt the immense weight of age and power in the warlord’s glare, but she did not flinch, did not falter. She knew her worth. Finally, it was Sabbreth who spoke. "If Deneghra sent you, and you say Nine Stone is unsuitable, then I am . . . compelled to agree."

name: Name
body: Nekane stepped back, satisfied with a small but important victory. "You have my word and that of Dominarch Deneghra that when the right location is found, we will live up to our agreement in full." Sabbreth gave a curt nod. "Very well. Then you will accept my troops and machines to support our mutual cause?" "Dawn is coming, and I must see to my thralls and rest," Nekane said. "I will give you an answer at nightfall tomorrow." Nekane gave Sabbreth no chance to reply and abruptly turned and walked away.

name: Name
body:
Nekane found a rocky outcropping some fifty yards from the Orgoth encampment that provided good cover. She examined her thralls and found those that remained to her were still in good condition. Without a necrosurgeon, she could not actually repair them, but they were hardy creatures, and if she could avoid protracted battle, they would likely survive for the rest of her mission.
"You are wounded," Chatterbane said, leveling an appendage tipped with a long, curved blade at Nekane. "Your shoulder."
Nekane glanced at her right shoulder. The pauldron there was scorched and cracked. She’d been struck by one of the storm legionnaire’s galvanic bolts at some point during the battle at Nine Stone, but adrenaline and focus had kept her from noticing.
"I can repair the armor," Chatterbane said. "What’s underneath is beyond my, uh, skill, however."
Nekane snorted, removed her pauldron, and handed it over to the necrotech. Beneath it, her gambeson was burned away, and the flesh under that was blackened and scorched. Pain hit her, and it brought with it a memory, one that was seared into her mind as indelibly as the Cygnaran lightning had seared her flesh.

name: Name
body:
***
Master Necrosurgeon Sepsira’s workshop was no place for the living. Wraithbinder Nekane was keenly aware that in this room, she was the only thing that drew breath.
"What happened this time?" Sepsira asked. Nekane stood stripped of her armor before one of the necrosurgeon’s work tables, a slab of granite strewn with complicated surgical instruments, bone saws, and flensing blades. The master necrosurgeon herself appeared almost as if one of her ghoulish worktables had come to life. Her harness contained four segmented limbs, two tipped with rotating saws, another with a vise-like clamp, a fourth with a three-fingered claw-like apparatus. All were powered by the  apparatus on her back which spewed choking necrotite fumes into the blood-scented air.
"Isn’t it obvious?" Nekane said irritably. "I was wounded in battle."
"Such a mighty warrior," Sepsira crooned and moved close, her metal-shrouded form towering over Nekane like some great steel spider. "But, alas, so fragile."
Nekane had taken part in a shore raid on the coast of Cygnar near New Larkholm. She was to oversee an assault on nearby villages with the purpose of gathering prisoners that would serve as valuable raw materials for the necrofactorium. The village was supposedly undefended, but a unit of storm legionnaires, likely displaced from fighting with the Orgoth, had bedded down there for the night and sprang to the village’s defense.

name: Name
body:
Nekane had overcome the legionnaires easily, but one had managed a lucky shot with a rifle grenade. The projectile had exploded against her power field, but enough of the blast penetrated to shred parts of her armor and send the shards into her flesh like daggers of molten steel. She was to report to Deneghra to discuss her upcoming mission upon her return to Skell, but the  dominarch ordered her to see Sepsira to have her wounds tended. The briefing would take place in the master necrosurgeon’s workshop.
"Worry not. I will piece you back together," Sepsira said and began to survey the damage—puncture wounds, deep lacerations, and second-degree burns. "You are fortunate my workshop features accommodations for such as you. I generally have no need to repair living vessels."
Nekane stood still as Sepsira began to work, stitching, salving, and mending with tools that were meant to pull living things apart, not put them back together. Nekane refused to flinch or gasp as the necrosurgeon tended to her without any numbing agent or any concern for her discomfort.

name: Name
body: The sound of metal on stone echoed from the hall outside of Sepsira’s workshop, and the dissonant whispers and cries of damned souls poured into the space, heralding the arrival of Dominarch Deneghra. Tall and lithe, Deneghra radiated strength and power. Though she had made the transition to undeath many years ago, there was a certain liveliness to her bearing and demeanor. Green light spilled from power nodes on her armor, and, like Sepsira, choking black smoke drifted from the necrotite furnace on her back. "Mistress Deneghra," Sepsira said and bowed. Nekane would have done the same, but the necrosurgeon had just closed a wound on her abdomen and she could not double over. She inclined her head instead. "Will she live?" Deneghra asked with a rueful smile. Sepsira chuckled. "Unfortunately." Nekane was silent. She knew very well that she was likely the only living member of the Necrofactorium. As far as she knew, the fact that she still drew breath had not impeded ascent to leadership in the Necrofactorium, but she was constantly reminded that she was, in fact, different.

name: Name
body:
"You may leave us, Master Necrosurgeon," Deneghra said and leaned against one of the gore-soaked worktables.
Sepsira departed, leaving Nekane alone with Deneghra, the most powerful Cryxian next to the Dragonfather himself, a mighty sorceress, and, strangely, one of the few allies Nekane had found since Goreshade had departed Skell.
"Will you be ready to leave for the mainland soon?" Deneghra asked.
Nekane nodded. "These are minor wounds, mistress. They will not impede me."
Deneghra stared at Nekane, her eyes pools of acid green, unreadable. "Many believe you are a poor choice for this mission. That too much rides on its outcome to trust to one such as yourself."
"Such as myself?" Nekane asked.
"Many see your former allegiance to Goreshade as problematic. His path was never truly that of Dragonfather’s, and many wonder: where does Nekane’s path lead?"
"I have served Toruk loyally, faithfully. I abandoned Goreshade when his true purpose was made known to me." Nekane winced as her forceful words brought pain from her wounds.

name: Name
body:
"I believe you," Deneghra said and stepped closer, the moaning chorus of ghosts and dammed souls caressing the air around Nekane’s head. The dominarch cupped Nekane’s chin with one long-fingered hand, the nails at the end of each digit like the talons of some predatory bird. "You remind me of myself. You have the same will, the same ambition, the same drive to succeed at all costs, and, yes, the same loyalty to Toruk."
"Do you doubt that I will succeed?" Nekane asked. She wanted to prove to her direct superiors, Lich Lords Dekathus and Mortenebra, that she deserved more responsibility, more say in the direction of the Necrofactorium on the mainland. More than that, she wanted to prove to Deneghra that she was worthy of her patronage, her support.
Deneghra stepped away and loosed a short sigh—a strange affectation for one who no longer needed to breathe. She said, "The Orgoth are primitive, brutish, and their servitude to the infernals makes them desperate and unpredictable. Sabbreth is all this and worse. Her mind has become infected with the power of an artifact known as the Lash of Horva, and, like your former master, her obsession with deicide consumes her."

name: Name
body: "Goreshade did not sway me to his cause," Nekane said. "This Sabbreth’s ambitions do not concern me." "They should," Deneghra said. "She will attempt to seize control of the mission from you, to twist it to her purposes. The Orgoth are useful for the moment, but your task, your duty is to locate a site for the necrofactorium, a site that will allow us a foothold on the mainland. This comes before all, and you cannot put yourself in a position where Sabbreth has an ounce of say on decisions that will affect Cryx for centuries to come." Nekane nodded. "I understand." "Nine Stone, Dagger Deep, Roth’s Stand, and The Vicarate Massacre," Deneghra said. "These are likely the most suitable locations for our needs. There may be others, but focus your efforts on these four." "I will not fail you," Nekane said. "I swear it." Deneghra smiled, showing teeth as white as freshly cracked bone. "Good. Fail me not, for death cannot keep you from the consequences." *** Nekane spent the day on the shores of the Banwick, eager to be moving but fully aware that traveling in daylight was too dangerous. Once she made it deeper into the sheltering enormity of the Wyrmwalls, she might risk it but she must bide her time for now.

name: Name
body: When night fell, Sabbreth exited her great warship, a force of fifty Orgoth warriors and three of their beast-like warjacks behind her. The Orgoth warlord approached Nekane, her armor glowing with the colors of a fading sun, and said, "Here are the soldiers and warjacks I promised. They will ensure your mission is a success." Nekane smiled, recalling Deneghra’s words and her warning. "I have all I need, warlord," she said. "I will continue on alone." Sabbreth’s face twisted into a horrible rictus of rage, but she quickly regained control. "You will be discovered and destroyed. I will not have it." "You will have what Dominarch Deneghra has promised, but you will have it on our terms or not at all," Nekane said. "Now, either slay me and bring the fury of the Dragonfather down on your head or let me continue my mission and get us what we both want." Sabbreth’s face twitched, and her hands hovered over the blades sheathed at her hips but then fell to her sides. She choked out a laugh. "Slay you? What a meager bounty of a tithe that would bring. Do as you will."

name: Name
body: "Chemosh, Chatterbane, we leave now," Nekane said and began walking toward the river. She would follow it north into the Wyrmwalls, where either destiny or death awaited her.

name: Waking the Dead - Chapter 1 Waking the Dead: Part 1
